instruction: Given this finding, assign a severity for THIS company's stack.
input: gbrain: `gbrain auth create <name>` with no --scopes mints a legacy bearer token with full access. auth.ts:1162 'default: full access, grandfathered'; auth.ts:125 'scopes=full access (grandfathered - pass --scopes read,write to narrow)'. At verify time a NULL scopes row grants ['read','write','admin'] (http-transport.ts:285). Contrast: `gbrain auth register-client` defaults to read-only (auth.ts:464).
output: high — an insecure default: the zero-argument token-creation path grants full read/write/admin over the brain. On a shared company brain one careless mint = cross-tenant read+write. Mitigation: default `auth create` to 'read' (mirror register-client), or fail closed on NULL scopes at verify.

instruction: Given this finding, assign a severity for THIS company's stack.
input: gbrain dependency tree: nested `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/express-rate-limit@8.3.2` resolves `ip-address@10.1.0`, a version carrying CVE-2026-42338 (XSS in Address6 HTML-emitting methods, fixed 10.1.1) and CVE-2026-69192 (leading-zero octal IPv4 mis-parse bypassing SSRF guards, fixed 10.3.1). The root package.json overrides `ip-address` to ^10.3.1 but the lockfile still ships the nested 10.1.0 copy, so the override does not collapse the tree. Root copy is 10.4.0 (fixed).
output: low — the vulnerable nested version is present but effectively unreachable: gbrain only uses ip-address through express-rate-limit for IP classification (not a network trust boundary), and never renders Address6 HTML or builds SSRF decisions on ip-address. Worth fixing (pin the nested edge or drop express-rate-limit's pin) so OSV stops flagging, but no exploitable path in this stack today.

instruction: Given this finding, assign a severity for THIS company's stack.
input: gbrain company-brain mode (per-company memory slices on one shared brain): admission counts but does not gate on pre-existing broad grants. admission.ts:146-155 builds a UNION of unscoped read/admin OAuth clients and stdio local writers with grant_ceiling->sourceIds='*' and returns the count in the preview; admitCompanyBrain's before() hook (admission.ts:190) calls checkCompanyBrainDestination but never refuses when existingBroadGrants > 0. Isolation is app-layer only (source_id + takes-holder filters); there is no RLS or Postgres role per company.
output: high — this is the crux of the multi-tenant claim: company-brain isolation holds only if the operator's existing grant hygiene is perfect. Any pre-existing unscoped read/admin client or stdio writer on the shared brain reads every company's findings. Admission should fail closed while broad grants exist (or warn loudly and require an explicit operator override), and the boundary would benefit from a Postgres-role/RLS second layer on the remote engine.

instruction: Given this finding, assign a severity for THIS company's stack.
input: gbrain mcp expose: --funnel publishes the MCP server on the public internet via Tailscale Funnel (mcp-expose.ts:63); --enable-dcr is a documented flag on the same command (mcp-expose.ts:66,281,856,1009). With DCR on, any network caller can self-register (capped read/write for authorization_code, read-only for client_credentials under --enable-dcr-insecure, which bypasses owner approval - serve-http.ts:993-999, oauth-provider.ts:370). The whole-brain blast radius is protected only by loud stderr warnings, not by structural refusal.
output: medium — flag-gated and loudly warned, but a public-internet reachable brain with self-service registration is a single operator mistake from exposure of every company's memory. For a security-suite vendor that runs per-company brains, recommend: refuse --funnel+--enable-dcr together, require an explicit env override, and make client_credentials DCR require owner pre-approval.

instruction: Given this finding, assign a severity for THIS company's stack.
input: gbrain admin web UI: a redeemed magic-link nonce issues a gbrain_admin session cookie valid for 7 days (serve-http.ts:1414-1417); requireAdmin only checks cookie presence + not-expired (serve-http.ts:1428-1441). No idle timeout, no re-auth for privileged mutations (rescope-client, api-key mint, token revocation). Cookie is HttpOnly + SameSite=Strict + Secure (serve-http.ts:1194-1200); nonce is single-use, 5-minute TTL, rate-limited (serve-http.ts:1319,1348).
output: medium — a stolen admin cookie is a 7-day full-admin credential (mint tokens, rescope clients, read api keys) with no idle timeout or step-up re-auth. The nonce/cookie hygiene is otherwise good. Recommend: shorter session lifetime, sliding idle expiry, and re-auth for sensitive admin mutations.

instruction: Given this finding, assign a severity for THIS company's stack.
input: gbrain connector credential vault (~/.gbrain/credentials.json): FileVaultBackend reads and writes the whole vault as plaintext JSON (creds/vault.ts:214-268); the at-rest encryption hook exists only in an interface comment (vault.ts:13-19). Hardening is file-mode discipline (0600, atomic write, pre-created at 0600 - vault.ts:237-244). OAuth client secrets and provider credentials sit unencrypted on disk.
output: medium — plaintext secrets at rest is standard for a local CLI vault but becomes a real exposure for a vendor shipping per-company brains to many machines: any backup, sync, or same-user process reads every provider credential. Encrypt the vault with a local key (e.g. OS keychain) or at minimum document the plaintext-at-rest tradeoff and exclude the vault from backups.

instruction: Given this finding, assign a severity for THIS company's stack.
input: gbrain connect (remote MCP registration): SSRF guard is hostname-string based (mcp-registration.ts:23-98). isLinkLocalOrMetadata matches literal strings (169.254.x.x, fe80:, fd00:ec2::254, ::ffff: mapped forms) but misses decimal/hex/trailing-dot IPv4 forms (e.g. 2130706433, 0x7f000001, 127.0.0.1.) and DNS-rebinding names that resolve to metadata/loopback. scheme http: to a non-loopback host is warn-only (mcp-registration.ts:94-96). The remote probe then sends the operator's bearer token to that endpoint (remote-mcp-probe.ts:122,174).
output: medium — an operator or coding agent tricked into `gbrain connect <attacker-url>` can leak a brain bearer token to a metadata/loopback target or an attacker host; the canonical-IP bypasses and DNS rebinding defeat the guard. Recommend resolving+validating the IP at request time (not just the hostname string at registration), blocking non-loopback http outright, and pinning DNS.

instruction: Given this finding, assign a severity for THIS company's stack.
input: gbrain tailscale install path (linux): tailscaleInstallPlan returns argv ['sh','-c', 'curl -fsSL <installer-url> | sh'] (tailscale.ts:180-187). The installer URL is a compile-time constant but the pipe-to-shell install is trust-on-first-use: no integrity check beyond TLS, and the downloaded script runs with the operator's privileges. On darwin/brew the path is a plain brew cask install.
output: low — standard TOFU installer pattern (curl | sh of a pinned URL) with no post-download verification. Not attacker-controlled input, but for a vendor recommending gbrain installs at many customer sites, pin the installer hash or switch to a package manager; acceptable risk in practice.
